title: Internal admin API and support tooling
goal: Give Centcom staff a small, tightly controlled internal admin API for support: look up users, workspaces and subscriptions (metadata only), revoke access, manage flags and status incidents, with every call audited and no ability to read content or impersonate.
scope_in: Internal-only Fastify plugin mounted under `/internal/admin/v1` on a separate listener (`ADMIN_API_PORT`) reachable only via the private network; disabled unless `ADMIN_API_ENABLED=true`.

Staff authentication: access token with scope `admin` AND membership in table `staff_users` with role `support_ro`, `support_rw` or `superadmin`; step-up header `X-Admin-Reason` (10-500 chars) and optional `X-Admin-Ticket` mandatory on every call.

Read endpoints: `GET /users/{id}` and `GET /users?email=`, `GET /workspaces/{id}` (members, roles, plan, subscription status, entitlements, usage totals), `GET /sessions/{id}` metadata (state, region, member count, timestamps), `GET /staff-audit`.

Write endpoints (support_rw+): revoke a device or all refresh-token families of a user, disable a user login, end a session (metadata action), resend an invite, call `grantPromotion` (B079), set/delete flags via the B083 service, create/update status incidents via the B086 service.
Response redaction: emails masked (`a***@d***.com`) for `support_ro`; no ciphertext, history, key material, join tokens, API key secrets, webhook secrets or payment data in any response.
Audit: every request writes an audit event with `actor_type:'staff'`, reason, ticket, target, outcome; staff audit endpoint lists them.
scope_out: Metadata search (B089); this lane mounts nothing for it but exposes the staff auth preHandler `requireStaff` it will use.
Impersonation / acting as a user: explicitly forbidden and not built.
The public RBAC matrix (B021) and the audit emitter implementation (B036); this lane consumes them.
Billing mutations beyond promotion grants (Stripe dashboard remains the tool for refunds).
build_against: Testkit factories for users/workspaces/sessions (B010), the audit emitter test double (B036), and fake services for flags, status and promotions behind interfaces; staff tokens minted by test helpers.
interfaces: Types exported from `apps/api/src/modules/admin/types.ts` (request/response DTOs) for the admin console.
Table `staff_users(user_id PK, role, added_by, added_at, disabled_at)`.
Config: `ADMIN_API_ENABLED`, `ADMIN_API_PORT`, `ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDRS`; rate limit 60 requests/min per staff user.
acceptance: A normal user token (without scope `admin`), a token with scope `admin` but no `staff_users` row, and a disabled staff user each receive 403 `forbidden`; no data is returned.
A request without `X-Admin-Reason` (or shorter than 10 chars) returns 422 and writes a denied audit event.

Every successful and denied call writes exactly one audit event containing actor, reason, ticket, target id and outcome; there is no code path that returns data without writing the event (test enumerates all routes).
`support_ro` gets masked emails and receives 403 on every write route; `support_rw` can write but cannot add staff or change roles; only `superadmin` can.

`GET /sessions/{id}` returns only metadata fields (id, workspace, state, region, created_at, ended_at, member_count, host member id); a JSON scan of all responses finds no field named `ct`, `p`, `secret`, `token`, `key_bundle`, or values with prefix `cen_live_`.
`POST /users/{id}/revoke-tokens` makes the user's next refresh attempt fail with `token_revoked` and the device sockets close with 4401 within 60 s.
The listener refuses connections from outside `ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDRS` (connection-level test) and the plugin is not registered when disabled (404 on the public listener).
More than 60 calls/min from one staff user returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
tests: authz matrix: roles x routes x token types, including expired and wrong-audience tokens.
audit completeness test enumerating all registered routes.
redaction test: JSON scan with forbidden field/value patterns on every read route.
integration: revoke-tokens then refresh fails; flag set then `GET /v1/flags` reflects it.
failure-path: dependency service (flags/status) down -> 502-class problem+json, audit event with outcome `error`.
negative: attempts to call any route with a user-supplied `workspace` header or impersonation parameter are rejected.
guardrails: MUST NOT implement impersonation, user-token minting, or any way to read session content, history, snapshots, keys, or message text.
MUST require a reason on every call and MUST audit reads as well as writes (support access to PII is itself sensitive).
MUST be unreachable from the public listener and the public load balancer; never mounted on the same port as `/v1`.
MUST NOT return secrets (API keys, webhook secrets, refresh tokens, Stripe ids beyond a masked tail) in any response.
MUST NOT allow staff to modify their own role or to act on their own staff record.
MUST fail closed when the audit write fails: the action is rolled back and 503 returned.
failure_modes: Audit store unavailable -> all admin calls fail with 503; no un-audited access.
Staff user removed mid-session -> next request denied (staff table checked each request, cache <= 5 s).
Target not found -> 404 with audit outcome `error`.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: the `admin` scope is declared 'internal only' in CT-AUTH but nothing defines how it is issued; this lane assumes an internal IdP/allow-listed login produces it, tracked as an operational decision. Admin routes are not part of any public contract and are excluded from the OpenAPI document. `implements` is empty because the internal API realises no wire contract.
